Regarding Ceylon [Sri Lanka] From Coromandel [Coromandel Coast] on the 31st of October in the year 1720. Register of such letters and papers as have been addressed today by the Esteemed Lord Gerrit Westrenen, governor and director of this Coast of Coromandel with the jurisdiction thereof, together with the council from Nagapatnam [Nagapatnam] over Ceylon to the Most Esteemed Lord Henric Zwaarde Croon, Governor-General, and the Esteemed Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies at Batavia [Jakarta], namely:

No. 1. Original missive to and from as in the heads of this of today's date
2. Copy of letters to and from as above per the ship Bellevliet [Bellevliet] dated the 10th of September, sent
3. Missive now to the Esteemed, Most Respected Lords Directors at the meeting of the Seventeen [the governing body of the VOC] to be forwarded per the return ships from Ceylon to Coromandel on the 31st of October in the year 1720, with the register of attachments annexed
No. 4. Separate letter from the Esteemed Lord Governor Gerrit Westrenen, written to His High Excellency the Governor-General Henric Zwaarde Croon
5. Patrimonial accounts [financial statements] of returns from this Government for the current ending year 1720, with the responses noted in the margin, annexed with two statements of the collected, sent, and remaining returns to indicate the entire procurement account of this year against those of the past year
6. Provisional responses to patrimonial accounts for the year 1721
7. Indian response accounts of linen goods from this ending year
8. Formal accounts of silver, gold, merchant provisions, and other necessities, etc., for Coromandel and the coming year 1721
9. Nine pieces of accounts of sold merchandise from Coromandel on the 31st of October in the year 1720. Merchandise and other goods at this Coast, namely: 3 pieces from Nagapatnam [Nagapatnam] from the months of July, August, and September; 3 pieces from Masulipatnam [Masulipatnam] from the months of June, July, and August, which have departed from there to Batavia with the Bellevliet. 2 pieces from Palliacatta [Palliacatta] from

From Coromandel on the 31st of October 1720

To the Most Esteemed Lord Henric Swaarde Croon, Governor-General, and the Esteemed Lords Councillors of the Netherlands Indies,

Lord and Esteemed Lords,

In continuation of our humble letter of the 9th of September last, which was sent to Your High Excellency regarding Masulipatnam [Masulipatnam], of which the copy is herewith annexed, we shall now supply as briefly as possible what was still lacking in the previous regarding the gifts made, speaking of carpentry and repairs, and also the weights that have fallen short on the merchandise, etc., at this Coast during the course of the account year 1717/20. Among these are some from the last half of 1719, which we shall nevertheless distinguish from the others, and first of all show in general how, according to the decision of the 10th of January to those of Masulipatnam [Masulipatnam], it was permitted that a certain Eramine grave [uncertain: possibly a local official or merchant] from the Company's behalf there was allowed to have the necessary repairs done to the Company's lodge within Golconda [Golconda] at the amount of 45 rupees [modern equivalent: approximately 45 rupees] 23/32, according to the statement of the Brahmin who has oversight thereof, provided that they would investigate once whether the same person was acting in good faith, since he continually comes forward with this and that carpentry work. The aforementioned overseer has also advised that a certain Brahmin and doctor of the Subah's [Subah: a provincial governor] mother had a sprout dug from the Company's water canal, and he complained about it to the regents but received no hearing, whereupon they have been ordered there to protest against it, or otherwise

--- CHUNK 1 ---
faithfully acts, while continually coming forward with various repairs, the aforementioned overseer has also advised that a certain Brahmin, and doctor of the Subah's mother had a sprout—from there reported to have had dug from the Company's water canal—a sprout, and he complained about this to the regents regarding the water, but received no hearing, whereupon they have been ordered there to have had to protest, or use other permitted means, which might be able to prevent the same, according to resolution of the 4th of July; the same Brahmin, has according to his report, also had to demolish a wall for the improvement of the aforesaid water canal within the Lodge; regarding this a certain merchant had complained to the regent, who had sent him a Subahdar [local official] to prevent it, but with the spending of a rupee, and in repairing the small garden to the extent that they were hindered by a certain Moor, who extends [his property] and pretends to a sum of 12 pagodas [modern equivalent: gold coins] per year from our decision of Coromandel on the 31st of October in the year 1720: the demonstration of its necessity was no further hindrance brought to him therein, while at Masulipatnam they wished to have a fence repaired at the fence on the upper side of the head's small garden situated, they encountered opposition there from the wife and brother-in-law of the Moor whose milk-field [uncertain: melkejie] whose property extends there against it, and also claimed a right of ownership thereto, from which they did not wish to desist unless they would be bought out with an annual rent of 12 pagodas; the heads N N [names not provided] have brought this offer before us, and believed that it was also not to be rejected, since the Company's Lodge would then in its entirety—from all surrounding dwellings, and thereby—from

there the milk-field whose property extends against it, and also claimed a right of ownership thereto, from which they did not wish to desist unless they would be bought out with an annual rent of 12 pagodas; the heads N N [names not provided] have brought this offer before us, and believed that it was also not to be rejected, since the Company's Lodge would then in its entirety—from all surrounding dwellings, and thereby—from all fire and inconveniences from outside would be freed and secured. The first matter we have regarded as a settled affair, since we could not judge of the necessity or non-necessity thereof, and it is also of little consequence; but regarding the latter we have deemed it more advisable and judged the Masulipatnam servants—to order that they should rather attempt once, or whether that property is not once for all for sale at a civil price, if so, our wall to Palicol [modern equivalent: Pallicol, a VOC settlement] to amount to for the one bearing. (this is the same wall which after the date was overturned by the people of Ramarasoe,) and those costs were borne the one by the Honored Company, and the other half by the inhabitants, since these—through the two years' duration of time around that place,

Item the Corps de Garde at the Amsterdam gate likewise required a completely unavoidable repair, whereupon by resolutions of 12 April, 24 May, and 20 September it was deemed advisable to have these put to work at the earliest, the first at the cost of approximately 18 pagodas [modern equivalent: Indian currency] and 20 [uncertain: unit of currency], the other of 21 pagodas and 5 famuns [modern equivalent: Indian currency subdivision], and the last of approximately 20 pagodas and 14¼, in the confidence that the one and the other shall be with your High Excellency's approval, which we humbly request thereupon, sent by this [uncertain: word unclear], and repaired. Item those sent to the small boats [chialoupen: small rowing vessels]. From Coromandel [Coromandel Coast] the 31st of October in the year 1720. The four small boats under this government, which are the small boats sailing, were in the month of October of the previous year all shortly one after another sent from here to Jaffna [Jaffnapatnam] to be sent there, in order to overwinter there, and to have their defects repaired; of which we gave the necessary pre-notice to the Honorable Lord Governor Isaac Augustijn Rumpf and council at Colombo [Colombo] also by a letter of the 16th of September, with the request to be willing to grant the necessary orders thereto to the Honorable Commandeur and council at Taffanapatnam [Taffanapatnam], which was also done, and so that the necessary supplies for the Liev and Eddemonij [ship names] well after repair of the one extra repair required, was then given to me and the Lier where the same from here

Isaac Augustijn Rumpf and council at Colombo also gave the necessary pre-notice by a letter of the 16th of September, with the request to be willing to grant the necessary orders thereto to the Honorable Commandeur and council at Taffanapatnam, which was also done, and so that the necessary supplies for the Liev and Eddemonij well after repair of the one extra repair required, was then given to me and the Lier where the same from here was also given, besides the usual pitch, tar, rope, soot, and other small items of rope-work, sail yarn, et cetera for the relief of minor defects, and the careening necessary for the small boat Eddemonij: 30 pieces of jati [teak] planks of 1½ inches, 2 bow timbers, 15 [uncertain: unit], and from Coromandel the 31st of October in the year 1720. 340 pounds [modern equivalent: Dutch pounds] of Dutch nails. The Maria: 20 pieces of jati planks of 1 inch. The Lier: 300 pieces of jati planks of 1 inch, 15 [uncertain: unit], 15 [uncertain: unit] of swalpen [uncertain: type of timber], 30 [uncertain: unit] of tincanse [uncertain: type of timber] planks, 6 [uncertain: unit] of palisade, and 4 [uncertain: unit] of maroedoe [uncertain: type of timber] timbers, 2000 pounds of Dutch nails, 200 [uncertain: unit] of [uncertain: unit] staav iron [uncertain: type of iron], 1 piece of anchor rope, and ½ [uncertain: unit] of Dutch wand [uncertain: measurement] of 6 inches. But upon undertaking that work at Jaffnapatnam it was actually found that there were considerably more defects, principally on the Lier and Codemonij, than had been guessed here, as the accompanying copy report shows, wherefore upon the further request of those friends by letters of the 25th of January here also in copy attached, on the 11th of February we sent further there: 17 pieces of jati planks of 2 to 3 inches, 10 [uncertain: unit] of [uncertain: unit]. The aforementioned small boats have returned here: the Susanna and Maria on the 29th of January and 4th of February, the Eddemonij on the 20th of March, but the Lier on the 19th of September, because, with the fierce westerly winds blowing through and the river water that had run off, it could not be brought out before then. Now in this northern month it is sent so that it comes in the spring with a late [uncertain: meaning unclear], the Eddemonij from there this river fetched, et cetera. On the 24th of September last past, there arrived here in the afternoon at half past four o'clock at the roadstead the ship Voorburg [Voorburg], and that same evening the bookkeeper came ashore, delivering to us the esteemed writings from our respective lords, the governors of Masulipatnam [Masulipatnam], from which it became clear to us that Their Excellencies had sent to this trading post for commerce and such purposes 6,000 pagodas [pagodas: Indian currency] in ready cash, namely 5,000 pagodas in gold and 1,000 in copper coinage.
